newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Kruger park devastated by fire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Kruger park devastated by fire.

text.p: A raging bush fire has devastated at least a quarter of South Africa's premier tourist attraction, the Kruger National Park game and nature reserve, officials said on Wednesday.
Thousands of animals and birds had probably died in the conflagration, the worst in over 40 years, the park said.
Authorities at the Kruger, which draws 700,000 tourists annually, said the blaze was sparked by lightning a week ago, compounded this week by high temperatures and gale force winds.
"It went out of control, there was nothing we could do. It's still burning now," spokesman Chris van der Linde told Reuters.
"This is the worst fire we've had since 1955."
The park, founded in 1926, covers 20,000 sq km (7,700 sq miles) of natural African bush half the size of Switzerland, and has the greatest diversity of wildlife of any park in the world.
Kruger's statistics are impressive: 336 species of indigeneous trees, 112 species of shrubs, more than 1,000 herb species and a profusion of flowers after seasonal rains.

It has 147 different species of mammals and 510 bird species, ranging from turkey-like ground hornbills to orange-eyed, shimmering starlings as well as 120,000 impala, 7,500 elephant, 900 leopards and more than 200 cheetah.
Van der Linde said the blaze had charred 25 percent of the park around the Satara camp in the southern part of the Kruger.
"A large number of animals are likely to be burnt to death," he said.
"The highest mortality of all the animals will probably be the impala because they are the most densely populated in that area."

Smaller mammals, tortoises and insects are also likely to be affected, raising concerns for the park's bio-diversity. Van der Linde said, however, the extent of the loss of animal life would only be known when the smoke cleared and fire dampened.
